title: Pre-warm demand forecast pool proposal for customer-POC
content:
Purpose:

Quick-working proposal for a hybrid pre-warm + predictive autoscaling pool for Customer-POC (internal alias: FinSight) — goal is to meet 99th%-tile latency SLOs during bursts while minimizing idle GPU costs for dedicated pools. This is a lightweight workshop artifact; not final architecture.

Background / customer constraints (from discovery):
- FinSight is testing generator-heavy features (assistant + summarization) with mixed traffic: daytime enterprise peaks and long-tail asynchronous bursts (scheduled nightly batches).
- Required SLO: p99 < 450ms for 256-token responses for interactive routes; background batch jobs can be slower.
- Expected concurrency profile for POC: baseline 150 req/min sustained, peak bursts up to 1200 req/min for <10 minute windows.
- Model mix: 60% LLM-v1 (quantized 4-bit), 30% LLM-v2 (fp16 distil), 10% reranker (small).
- KV-cache expected to improve cost on repeated prompts: assume 25% effective prefix cache hit in steady-state, drops to 5% during brand-new-burst traffic.
- Security: Dedicated pool required (no multi-tenant sharing for this customer).

Design goals / constraints:
- Make tradeoff between warm capacity (idle cost) and cold-start latency.
- Use predictive scaling to pre-warm GPUs when forecast shows imminent burst (based on 5–15 min horizon).
- Maintain graceful degradation: fallback to lower-cost model variant (LLM-v1-quantized) for non-critical traffic when under-provisioned.
- Keep ops complexity low: prefer components we already have in Redwood (autoscaler hooks + routing policies).

Proposal summary (high-level):
1) Hybrid pool split: pre-warm pool (small, always-on), dynamic autoscaling pool (reacts to live load), and a cold standby group (paused; can be spun up with burst policy).
   - Pre-warm pool: 2 x A100-80GB equivalent (or 6 x L4 depending on customer preference) to keep p99 for small sustained load and to serve immediate burst headroom.
   - Dynamic pool: minimum 0, scale up to N based on target throughput and predicted arrivals.
   - Cold standby: snapshot images ready to attach, warm boot target 2–4 minutes (acceptable for background jobs).

2) Predictive autoscaler algorithm: lightweight: EWMA on recent request rate + weekday/time-of-day multiplier + rapid detection of 2x jumps. If forecasted short-term demand (next 5 min) > current capacity * target_util, pre-warm additional GPUs.
   - target_util set to 65% of per-GPU token throughput to keep p99 headroom.
   - Use short-term forecast window (5 min) for pre-warm decisions, longer window (30 min) for scale-out to dynamic pool.

3) Warm-up strategy and routing: when pre-warming, route lower-SLA/low-cost variants to cold capacity and reserve pre-warm for interactive SLO-bound requests. Include automatic KV-cache priming by replaying a small sample of recent hot prefixes (privacy check: only synthetic or customer-approved samples).

4) Fallbacks: automated model-fallback route policy prioritizing availability over fidelity. If capacity constrained, switch 20–40% of traffic to quantized variant with instrumentation to track quality drop.

Assumptions for cost model (base numbers intentionally conservative):
- GPU hourly on-demand equivalent costs (Redwood internal pricing):
  - A100-80GB equiv: $3.20 / GPU / hr
  - H100 equiv: $5.90 / GPU / hr (higher perf; use only if required)
  - L4 equiv: $0.70 / GPU / hr (low cost, good for quantized models)
- System overhead (orchestration / storage / networking): 12% of GPU spend
- Average tokens produced per request: 160 tokens (response) + 20 input tokens = 180 total
- Tokens/sec per GPU (varies by model):
  - LLM-v1 quantized on L4: ~200 tokens/sec
  - LLM-v1 quantized on A100: ~720 tokens/sec (better batching/kernels)
  - LLM-v2 fp16 on A100: ~420 tokens/sec
- p99 safety factor: provision for 1.6x concurrency on top of average to protect latency SLOs

Quick scenario calc (sustained baseline + peak minutes):
Inputs: baseline 150 req/min, peak 1200 req/min for 8 minutes, mix as above, avg tokens 180.
1) Convert to tokens/sec:
   - baseline: 150 req/min * 180 tokens / 60 = 450 tokens/sec
   - peak: 1200 req/min * 180 / 60 = 3600 tokens/sec
2) Effective tokens/sec per GPU (weighted by model and cache): assume overall effective tok/s per A100 = 600 tok/s after accounting for model mix and cache drop during burst.
3) GPUs required (with p99 safety 1.6x):
   - baseline GPUs = ceil((450 / 600) * 1.6) = ceil(1.2) = 2 GPUs (matches pre-warm pool)
   - peak GPUs = ceil((3600 / 600) * 1.6) = ceil(9.6) = 10 GPUs total
   - Delta for dynamic scaling = 8 GPUs (10 - 2) to be scaled up during bursts.

Cost estimate (per-hour during patterns):
- If using A100 equiv for both pre-warm and dynamic:
  - Idle cost (pre-warm 2 GPUs): 2 * $3.20 = $6.40/hr + overhead => $7.17/hr
  - Peak cost (10 GPUs): 10 * $3.20 = $32.00/hr + overhead => $35.84/hr
  - For an 8-minute burst inside an hour: blended hourly = ( (8/60)*35.84 + (52/60)*7.17 ) = $11.05/hr on average that hour.
- If using L4 for pre-warm and A100 for dynamic:
  - Pre-warm 6 L4 equiv: 6 * $0.70 = $4.20/hr + overhead => $4.70/hr (gives similar p99 for small sustained loads)
  - Dynamic A100 usage only during burst: 8 GPUs * $3.20 = $25.60 + overhead => $28.67 for the 8-min window; blended similar calc => ~ $9.05/hr that hour.

Notes on cost tradeoffs: using many small L4 instances for pre-warm shifts cost to more network/packing overhead but saves A100 idle dollars. If the customer value curve favors low-cost idle (typical enterprise POC), L4 pre-warm + A100 dynamic is recommended. If model fidelity requires H100-class perf even for interactive SLOs, base numbers rise ~1.8x; we should only recommend H100 after perf benchmarking.

Operational runbook (sketch):
- Pre-warm autoscaler: maintain pre-warm target = 2 A100 (or 6 L4) always-on.
- Predictive autoscaler job (runs every 60s): compute EWMA forecast, if forecast > threshold, trigger pre-warm action: attach 2 GPUs (scale step) and start routing test traffic; continue until forecast satisfied or reach cap.
- Cold standby boot pipeline: keep images and kernel caches snapshot-ready; test boot periodically (weekly) to keep AMI warm.
- Observability: instrument per-model token/s, per-GPU util, cold-start latency histogram, cache-hit rates. Create alert: sustained util > 80% for 2 minutes => escalate to runbook to increase pre-warm target.

Quality / evaluation plan for POC:
- 1-week baseline: validate capacity math (measure effective tok/s per GPU under POC batch).
- Synthetic burst tests: 3x synthetic bursts (1200 req/min for 8–12 min) during business hours to validate scale-up time and p99 latency.
- Two canaries: model-fallback canary (10% traffic) to measure fidelity drop; pre-warm canary (route 5% of users to pre-warmed L4 path) to verify cache priming and hit rates.

Open questions / unknowns (action items):
- Exact token throughput per GPU for customer models — need perf runs with customer's model weights (ACTION: GH perf-job #42).
- Customer acceptance of quantized fallback for a portion of traffic (ACTION: Solutions AE to confirm with FinSight PM).
- Warm-boot time for cold standby on customer infra (ACTION: infra-eng to measure boot time on staging).
- Licensing/instance availability in customer-preferred region (ACTION: infra-supply check).

Immediate next steps to move POC forward:
- Schedule 2-hour workshop with customer + infra (owners: Aisha, Marcus).
- Spin up micro-benchmark with one A100 and one L4 using sample prompt set (owner: Diego).
- Draft SLA tradeoff one-pager for customer decision: cost vs p99 (owner: Sana).

Appendix: quick sensitivity notes
- If EV (expected burst frequency) increases (bursts > 3/hr), pre-warm more aggressively (3–4 A100 equiv) — cost grows linearly.
- If KV-cache can be primed to 40% effective hit on bursts, peak GPU need drops ~20% (re-run numbers).
- If customer prefers lower complexity: recommend simple min=2, max=12 reactive autoscale with 90s cooldown; will increase p99 risk for 0–90s of a sudden peak but reduces infra orchestration work.

Rough action item list (short):
- [ ] Perf benchmark runs (GH: #42) (Diego)
- [ ] Customer quantized-fallback acceptance (Sana)
- [ ] Infra boot time test (Marcus)
- [ ] Workshop scheduling (Aisha)
